==Problem== There are 24 four-digit whole numbers that use each of the four digits 2, 4, 5 and 7 exactly once. Only one of these four-digit numbers is a multiple of another one. Which of the following is it? \textbf{(A)}\ 5724 \qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 7245 \qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 7254 \qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 7425 \qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 7542 ==Solution 1== The smallest number formed from these four digits is 2457 while the largest is 7542. Since 7542 < 2457 \cdot 4, the correct answer must be either 2 or 3 times another number containing these four digits. By inspection, \boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 7425} is correct since 7425 \div 3 = 2475. (A) is incorrect since 5724 \div 2 = 2862 and 5724 \div 3 = 1908. (B) is incorrect since 7245 \div 3 = 2415. (C) is incorrect since 7254 \div 2 = 3627 and 7254 \div 3 = 2418. (E) is incorrect since 7542 \div 2 = 3771 and 7542 \div 3 = 2514. ~ M4ST3R0FM4TH with minor corrections from Pi-rate_X, edited by j314andrews ==Solution 2== Let ABCD and WXYZ be four-digit integers such that \{A, B, C, D\}=\{W, X, Y, Z\}=\{2,4,5,7\}, and WXYZ is a multiple of ABCD. As in solution 1, either ABCD \times 2 = WXYZ or ABCD \times 3 = WXYZ. Suppose ABCD \times 2 = WXYZ. Then A = 2, since otherwise ABCD \times 2 is too large. If D = 4 or D = 5, then Z = 8 or Z = 0 which is invalid. So D = 7 and Z = 4. Since W is at least 4 but less than 6, W = 5. If B = 4, 2 \times ABCD is too small, so B = 5. Thus C = 7 and ABCD = 2547. But in this case 2 \times ABCD = 5094, which is invalid. Thus ABCD \times 3 = WXYZ. Then A = 2, since otherwise ABCD \times 3 is too large. If B = 7, then ABCD > 2700 and WXYZ > 3 \times 2700 = 8100 which is too large. If D = 7, then Z = 1 which is invalid. So C = 7. If B = 4 and D = 5, then WXYZ = 3 \times 2574 = 7722 which is invalid. Therefore, B = 5 and D = 4, so WXYZ = 3 \times 2475 = \boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 7425}. -j314andrews ==Solution 3== Let ABCD and WXYZ be four-digit integers such that \{A, B, C, D\}=\{W, X, Y, Z\}=\{2,4,5,7\}, and WXYZ is a multiple of ABCD. As in solution 1, either ABCD \times 2 = WXYZ or ABCD \times 3 = WXYZ. Suppose ABCD \times 2 = WXYZ. Since ABCD \geq 2457, WXYZ \geq 2457 \times 2 = 4914. Note that 5274 is the smallest possible even value of WXYZ which is at least 4914, so WXYZ \geq 5274. Since WXYZ \leq 7542, ABCD \leq 7542 \div 2 = 3761. Note that 2754 is the largest possible value of ABCD which is at most 3761, so ABCD \leq 2754. Since ABCD \leq 2754, ABCD \leq 2754 \times 2= 5508. Note that 5472 is the largest possible even value of WXYZ which is at most 5508, so WXYZ \leq 5472. Since WXYZ \leq 5472, ABCD \leq 5472 \div 2 = 2736. Note that 2574 is the largest possible value of ABCD which is at most 2736, so ABCD \leq 2574. Since ABCD \leq 2574, WXYZ \leq 2574 \times 2 = 5148. But it is impossible for both WXYZ \geq 5274 and WXYZ \leq 5148, and thus ABCD \times 2 \neq WXYZ. Therefore, ABCD \times 3 = WXYZ. Since ABCD \geq 2457, WXYZ \geq 2457 \times 3 = 7371. Note that 7425 is the smallest possible value of WXYZ which is at least 7371, so WXYZ \geq 7425. Since WXYZ \leq 7542, ABCD \leq 7542 \div 3 = 2514. Note that 2475 is the largest possible value of ABCD which is at most 2514, so ABCD \leq 2475. Since ABCD \leq 2475, WXYZ \leq 2475 \times 3 = 7425. Since both WXYZ \geq 7425 and WXYZ \leq 7425, WXYZ = \boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 7425} (and thus ABCD = 7425 \div 3 = 2475). -j314andrews ==See Also== {{AMC8 box|year=2001|num-b=24|after=Last
